title: Same sepsis spec, three engines: where compute time goes
interpretation: Wall-clock for one matched 48 h severe-sepsis run of the SAME model specification, executed by three interchangeable engines. BioGears 8.2.0 (the original C++ whole-body physiology engine) takes ~3.38 h; the Tellurium/roadrunner exact-SBML extraction of the same core takes ~2.81 h (BioGears + Tellurium figures from study 04-engine-runtime, committed meta.wall_s). Both are dominated by the same cost: integrating the stiff 91-state ODE (study 06 shows a stiff implicit solver, CVODE, is required and already compiled C). A PyTorch neural surrogate of the same core runs the 48 h / 576-step rollout in ~0.2 s — roughly 40,000× faster than the exact SBML path (figure from the neural-surrogate-sepsis investigation) — because it replaces the ODE solve with one forward pass per step. The surrogate trades accuracy for speed (its stabilized form stays bounded over the full horizon but is not yet clinically accurate), so it is a fast approximate tier, not a drop-in replacement. The point of the figure is the span: the same spec runs across four-plus orders of magnitude of compute by swapping the engine, and the compute in the exact engines is spent almost entirely in stiff ODE integration.
caption: Two views of where the compute goes for the same sepsis spec. Left: full 48 h run wall-clock under BioGears (~3.38 h), Tellurium exact SBML (~2.81 h), and the PyTorch surrogate (~0.2 s) — committed numbers. Right: live per-step cost measured on this machine — one exact CVODE step of the real 91-state model ~528 ms vs one surrogate forward pass ~0.042 ms (exact is ~12,500×). Both show the same thing: the exact engines spend their time in the stiff ODE solve; the surrogate replaces it with a forward pass.
provenance: Left panel — BioGears + Tellurium: studies/04-engine-runtime (committed meta.wall_s, severe 48 h); surrogate: neural-surrogate-sepsis investigation (~0.2 s). Right panel — live per-step benchmark measured by bench_live.py (TelluriumProcess CVODE per interval on sources/biogears_sepsis.ant vs a viva-torch NeuralProcess forward pass), warm, written to bench_live.json. Chart script: make_runtime_compare.py.
